questions.definition: A base-16 number system that uses the values 0-9 and characters A-F.
questions.clue: Often used as a shorter way to write binary values.
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal uses sixteen symbols. Each hexadecimal digit represents four binary bits, which makes long binary values easier to read.

questions.definition: A base-2 number system that uses the values 0 and 1.
questions.clue: Computers store data using this system.
questions.explanation: Binary is used by computers because digital circuits can represent two states reliably, such as on and off.

questions.definition: Base 10 number system, how we normally count, using digits 0 to 9.
questions.explanation: Denary is the number system most people use in daily life. It has ten possible digits in each place value.

questions.definition: A code for representing English characters as numbers, with each character assigned a value from 0 to 127.
questions.explanation: ASCII represents letters, digits, punctuation, and control characters using numeric codes. Standard ASCII uses 7 bits.

questions.definition: A character code that enables most of the languages of the world to be represented with unique character identifiers.
questions.clue: Supports far more characters than ASCII.
questions.explanation: Unicode can represent characters from many writing systems, as well as symbols and emoji, making it suitable for global text.

questions.definition: An error that results when the number of bits is not enough to hold the number.
questions.clue: The value is too large for the available bits.
questions.explanation: Overflow happens when a calculation produces a value outside the range that can be represented with the available number of bits.

questions.definition: A method of representing negative numbers in the binary system.
questions.clue: The most significant bit indicates the sign.
questions.explanation: Two's complement allows computers to represent positive and negative integers and makes binary arithmetic with negative values simpler.

questions.definition: The dimensions of an image.
questions.clue: Often given as width by height.
questions.explanation: Image resolution describes how many pixels an image has horizontally and vertically, such as 1920 by 1080.

questions.definition: Additional data stored with an image, such as its dimensions or the time and date it was taken.
questions.explanation: Metadata gives extra information about a file. For images, it may include resolution, camera model, location, or date taken.

questions.definition: The number of bits used to create each colour in an image.
questions.clue: More bits allow more possible colours.
questions.explanation: Higher colour depth increases the number of colours that can be represented, but it also increases file size.

questions.definition: A small piece of sound recorded at regular time intervals.
questions.clue: Used when converting analogue sound to digital data.
questions.explanation: Sampling measures the amplitude of sound at regular intervals so the sound can be stored digitally.

questions.definition: The number of sound samples recorded each second.
questions.explanation: A higher sample rate captures more detail from the original sound, but it also increases file size.

questions.definition: The number of bits used to record each sound sample.
questions.explanation: Higher sample resolution records each sample more precisely, improving sound quality but increasing file size.

questions.definition: An image composed of pixels with a fixed resolution.
questions.explanation: Bitmap images are made from individual pixels. Enlarging them too much can make them appear pixelated.

questions.definition: The smallest measurement for data.
questions.explanation: A bit is a single binary digit. Larger units such as nibbles, bytes, and kibibytes are built from bits.

questions.definition: 4 bits or half a byte.
questions.clue: One hexadecimal digit is one of these.
questions.explanation: A nibble contains four bits, which is exactly enough to represent one hexadecimal digit.

questions.definition: 8 bits, enough for one letter in many English character encodings.
questions.explanation: A byte contains eight bits. File sizes and memory capacity are commonly measured using bytes and larger units.

questions.definition: 1024 bytes.
questions.explanation: A kibibyte is based on powers of 2, unlike a kilobyte in decimal notation, which is often treated as 1000 bytes.

questions.definition: 1024 kibibytes.
questions.explanation: A mebibyte is a binary unit of storage equal to 1024 KiB.

questions.definition: 1024 mebibytes.
questions.explanation: A gibibyte is a binary unit of storage equal to 1024 MiB.

questions.definition: 1024 gibibytes.
questions.explanation: A tebibyte is a binary unit of storage equal to 1024 GiB.

questions.definition: 1024 tebibytes.
questions.explanation: A pebibyte is a binary unit of storage equal to 1024 TiB.

questions.definition: 1024 pebibytes.
questions.explanation: An exbibyte is a binary unit of storage equal to 1024 PiB.

questions.definition: A method that uses an algorithm to reduce the size of a file.
questions.explanation: Compression reduces file size to save storage space or transmission time. Some methods preserve all data, while others remove data.

questions.definition: A compression method that reduces file size by permanently removing data.
questions.explanation: Lossy compression can greatly reduce file size, but some original data is lost and cannot be restored exactly.

questions.definition: A compression method that reduces file size without permanently removing data.
questions.clue: The original file can be restored exactly.
questions.explanation: Lossless compression preserves all original data, making it suitable where exact recovery is important.

questions.definition: A process used in lossy compression that removes sounds not normally heard by the human ear.
questions.clue: Used to reduce audio file size.
questions.explanation: Perceptual music shaping removes less noticeable sounds, such as sounds masked by louder ones, to reduce audio file size.

questions.definition: An algorithm that groups together repeating patterns and indexes them.
questions.explanation: Run Length Encoding stores repeated data as a value and a count, which can reduce the size of simple images or repeated sequences.

questions.definition: A fixed-layout document format that maintains its original appearance regardless of the software used to view it.
questions.clue: Often used for documents to share or print.
questions.explanation: PDF files preserve layout, fonts, and formatting, making them useful when documents need to look the same on different devices.

questions.definition: A lossy compressed file format commonly used for website images.
questions.explanation: JPG reduces image file size using lossy compression, which is useful for photos but can reduce quality if compressed heavily.

questions.definition: A compressed image format using only 256 colours, used for simple web graphics.
questions.explanation: GIF is suitable for simple graphics with limited colours, but it is not ideal for high-quality photographs.

questions.definition: A lossless compressed format using an alpha channel to preserve transparent backgrounds.
questions.clue: Often used when transparency is needed.
questions.explanation: PNG preserves image quality and can store transparency, making it useful for logos, icons, and web graphics.

questions.definition: A lossy compressed music format.
questions.explanation: MP3 reduces audio file size by removing less noticeable sound data, making it convenient for storing and streaming music.

questions.definition: A lossy compressed file format that can be used for audio and video and is appropriate for streaming.
questions.explanation: MP4 is widely used for video and audio because it balances file size, quality, and streaming compatibility.
